signals.signal: Full device census pulled from BCR's own public locations API on 30/07/2026 (types=ATM/MFM/BRANCH, unique ouIds): 1,096 cash-dispense ATMs and 573 multifunctional machines (MFM, cash-deposit capable) = 1,669 self-service devices; 284 branches, of which 212 tagged CASHLESS and 72 still tagged GHISEU (staffed teller counter); 236 branches have a 24/7 self-service zone; 62 branches offer business cash deposit (ADN, RON only); 27 offer video advisory. The 284-branch count exactly matches BCR's own H1 2026 results PDF of the same date, which validates the API as an accurate census.
signals.source_name: BCR branch/ATM locator API (bcr.ro GEM locations endpoint)
signals.implies: Hard, dated sizing of the addressable fleet. 1,096 cash-out-only ATMs are the recycler/MFM upgrade pool; only 573 of 1,669 devices (34%) take deposits today. Direct fit for Printec ATM/self-service hardware, cash recyclers, multivendor software and managed services. Corrects the baseline's '~2,000 machines / ~955 ATMs'.
signals.likelihood: Fleet is live today; refresh decisions likely inside 12 months given the fleet is contracting
signals.followup: Re-pull the same API monthly to track net device adds/removals and cashless-branch conversion; the OEM behind the MFM fleet is still unidentified - make that a standing task.

signals.signal: Accessibility gap quantified from the same 30/07/2026 API pull: only 376 of 1,096 ATMs (34%) carry the VOICE (audio guidance) tag, against 572 of 573 MFMs (99.8%); 73 ATMs are not tagged CONTACTLESS; only 320 ATMs dispense EUR. Romania's Law 232/2022 (transposing EU Accessibility Act, Directive 2019/882) applies to products placed on the market from 28/06/2025, and lets self-service terminals already in use before that date continue only until 28/06/2030 (and no more than 20 years in service).
signals.source_name: BCR locator API cross-read against Law 232/2022 (Lege5 consolidated text)
signals.implies: About 720 BCR ATMs lack audio guidance and must be remediated (audio-jack/software retrofit) or replaced before 28/06/2030 - a legally-forced, dated refresh pipeline for Printec ATM hardware, multivendor software and managed services. Peer pressure is visible: Raiffeisen Romania completed national ATM voice guidance in Q1 2026, so BCR is behind a direct competitor.
signals.likelihood: High that BCR must act well before 28/06/2030; budget lines likely 2027-2028
signals.followup: Establish whether the 720 non-voice ATMs are software-upgradeable or need hardware swap; look for a published BCR accessibility remediation timetable.

signals.signal: Fleet and footprint are BOTH contracting, quantified between two primary disclosures. Audited FY2025 annual report (filed to BVB 30/03/2026): 290 branches, 73% cashless, 81% with 24/7 self-service zones, 20 corporate business centres, 18 mobile offices, 'almost 2,000' ATM+multifunctional machines. Official H1 2026 results PDF (30/07/2026): 19 corporate business centres, 15 corporate mobile offices, 284 retail units, 74% cashless, 1,750 ATM+multifunctional machines. Net change over six months: -6 branches, -1 corporate centre, -3 mobile offices, -250 devices (-12.5% of the fleet).
signals.source_name: BCR Raport anual 2025 (BVB infocont) and BCR rezultate financiare Sem I 2026 (PDF)
signals.implies: A 250-device net reduction inside six months is an active rationalisation programme: low-throughput cash-out ATMs pulled while deposit-capable MFMs carry the load. This is the classic entry moment for recycler consolidation, cash-cycle optimisation and an opex ATM-as-a-service model - and the risk moment, because a shrinking fleet also shrinks any incumbent's service base.
signals.followup: Ask BCR IR for the split of the 1,750 between ATM and MFM at 30/06/2026. Note the bcr.ro English 'Our company' page is stale (318 units, 63% cashless, ~2,000 machines) - use RO pages, the H1 PDF and the API only.

signals.signal: Derived from the 30/07/2026 API pull by matching device coordinates to branch coordinates (4 decimal places): roughly 782 of 1,096 ATMs (71%) sit away from a BCR branch, versus 169 of 573 MFMs (29%). ATMs are present in 383 towns and MFMs in 173, against 157 towns with a branch.
signals.implies: An off-site estate of roughly 780 ATMs across 383 towns is exactly the asset class peers have handed to a partner - Piraeus to Cashflex/Printec, Banca Intesa Beograd to Payten, Raiffeisen Romania to Euronet, CrediaBank to Euronet. It is the single most sellable managed-services / ATM-as-a-service perimeter at BCR, and it is the perimeter most exposed to being lost to a rival deployer.
signals.likelihood: Outsourcing debate plausible within 12-24 months as fleet economics worsen
signals.followup: Coordinate matching is approximate (some in-branch lobby devices may be geocoded slightly apart) - treat 782/169 as an order of magnitude, and validate against BCR's own on-site/off-site split.

signals.signal: H1 2026 results published 30/07/2026: net profit RON 1,205m (EUR 234m), -18.2% y/y; operating result RON 2,116m (+1.6%); operating income RON 3,315m (+3.1%); net interest income RON 2,365m, slightly below H1 2025; net fee and commission income RON 632m (+15.5%); general administrative expenses RON 1,199m (+6.0%), attributed to inflation, the VAT increase, RON depreciation and 'continued investment in strategic initiatives'; cost/income 36.2%; net loans RON 73,015m; deposits RON 93,806m; NPL 2.9% with 133% coverage; total capital ratio 24.0%; RON 484m paid to the state budget including RON 200m of bank turnover tax.
signals.source_name: BCR press release, Grupul BCR Semestrul I 2026
signals.implies: Profit down 18% while opex is up 6% and a turnover tax bites. Management is under pressure to convert fixed branch cost into variable machine cost, which favours opex-based managed services over capex purchases.
signals.likelihood: Cost pressure certain into the 2027 budget cycle
signals.followup: Erste's Romania segment view for 1-6 2026: operating income EUR 551m, operating expenses EUR 233m, cost/income deteriorated to 42.3% from 40.0%, net result EUR 156m (-32.1%).

signals.signal: Erste Group H1 2026 interim report, note 31: on 06/04/2026 BCR received an investigation report from the Romanian Competition Council alleging coordinated fixing of the ROBOR reference rate among the ten panel banks since November 2018. Per the Competition Council Plenum meeting minutes the fine on BCR is 6.1875% of its 2025 turnover = RON 577,361,887 (~EUR 110m). The reasoned decision had not been served on BCR as at 30/07/2026; BCR will contest by all available legal means. Romanian press reports total sanctions of RON 3.73bn across ten banks announced 07/06/2026, with BNR publicly questioning the decision.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Interim Report H1 2026, note 31 Contingent liabilities - legal proceedings
signals.implies: A ~EUR 110m competition fine plus a multi-year appeal raises board-level appetite for demonstrable conduct and transaction surveillance, and raises the auditability bar on any outsourced service. Printec's AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring lines are the adjacency, though the specific conduct here is market-benchmark rather than payments fraud.
signals.likelihood: Litigation certain; compliance-spend uplift plausible within 12 months
signals.followup: Track the final reasoned decision and BCR's court challenge; consiliulconcurentei.ro was unreachable this run so the fine figure rests on Erste's own disclosure (which is the stronger source anyway).

signals.signal: Erste Group H1 2026 note 33: average weighted headcount of Banca Comerciala Romana Group fell to 4,966 in 1-6 2026 from 5,138 in 1-6 2025 (-172 FTE, -3.3% y/y).
signals.source_name: Erste Group Interim Report H1 2026, note 33 Average number of employees
signals.implies: Headcount falling faster than the branch count is the signature of teller-to-machine migration. The 72 branches still tagged with a staffed teller counter are the named remaining conversion pipeline for cash recyclers/TCRs and assisted-service kiosks.
signals.followup: Build the 72 GHISEU branches into a named TCR target list from the API output.

signals.signal: APTRA OptiSuite / OptiCash incumbency RE-VERIFIED against the vendor's own still-live newsroom page dated 23/03/2018: BCR deployed NCR's APTRA Cash Management Suite (OptiSuite) across a then 2,600+ ATM network and its cash processing centres, with PRINTEC named as NCR's channel partner on the project. Stated results: ATM replenishments -13.3%, branch cash transports -18.6%, zero emergency cash deliveries over nine months, 99.8% ATM availability. BCR then had 500+ branches and ~2,000 daily corporate cash pickup orders.
signals.source_name: NCR Atleos newsroom, 'Banca Comerciala Romana Improves Cash Management Efficiency with NCR Software'
signals.implies: Printec is already inside BCR's cash-management stack - the warm-lead route into the far larger 2026 conversations on fleet refresh, recycler conversion, accessibility remediation and multivendor managed services. It is equally the defensive priority: the reference is eight years old, the fleet it was sized for (2,600+) has shrunk to 1,669, and a re-bid is overdue.
signals.followup: Confirm internally whether the OptiSuite/OptiCash contract is still live, its renewal date, and whether cash forecasting now covers the 573 deposit-capable MFMs as well as the 1,096 ATMs. No 2019-2026 public re-confirmation of this contract was found this run - that gap is itself a risk flag.

signals.signal: George Business, BCR's SME/corporate platform, completed migration off the legacy eBCR and 24Banking BCR channels at the end of 2025 after roughly two years of phased transition. At H1 2026 it has over 11,000 corporate clients and processes EUR 12bn of transactions per month, which BCR describes as ~3% of Romania's annual GDP; reported alongside over 24,000 active users, more than 15,000 payment files uploaded monthly, files of up to 25,000 individual transactions, and 1.2 million statements generated monthly. From Q2 2026 over 8,800 clients have FX Pro (negotiated in-platform FX on 66 currency pairs); in June 2026, 85% of FX volumes ordered in George Business went through FX Pro.
signals.source_name: BCR press release Grupul BCR Semestrul I 2026 (client/volume figures) and iDevice.ro coverage of the George Business launch (migration detail)
signals.implies: A high-volume SME payments rail is the natural attach point for merchant acquiring/POS, real-time transaction monitoring and business cash automation. The white space is physical: only 62 of 284 branches accept business cash deposits at a machine (ADN) and only in RON, so 222 branches have no business-deposit automation at all - a clean smart-safe/business-recycler pitch.
signals.likelihood: Platform expansion continues; business cash-deposit gap persists
signals.followup: The legacy-decommission and 24,000-user/15,000-file figures come from press (iDevice.ro, 03/04/2026) reporting a BCR launch - re-confirm on a BCR page. Probe whether George Business adds merchant/POS or smart-safe modules.

signals.signal: MoneyGram remittance send-and-receive is enabled at the terminal on 572 of 573 BCR multifunctional machines; contactless card withdrawal is on all 573 MFMs and 1,023 of 1,096 ATMs; EUR withdrawal is on only 320 ATMs and 13 MFMs.
signals.implies: BCR already monetises the self-service channel beyond cash (remittances at the machine), which strengthens the business case for MFM density and for value-added application software on the terminal - a Printec multivendor-software and managed-services angle rather than pure hardware.
signals.followup: Check whether the MoneyGram integration is delivered through the ATM application layer (retrofittable to the 1,096 ATMs) or only the MFM platform.

signals.signal: Retail digital origination scale-up in H1 2026: 2.38 million active George mobile users; over 1 million retail products sold end-to-end digitally; over 40% of BCR mortgages taken on a 100% digital flow in George, versus 17% a year earlier, with property documents uploaded from the phone and validated immediately and approval-to-signature in as little as 5 working days; 93% of new insurance sales digital; 98% of Pillar III pension enrolments digital; 98% of retail investment transactions digital; over 107,000 clients completed the investment knowledge-and-experience test.
signals.source_name: BCR press release, Grupul BCR Semestrul I 2026
signals.implies: Instant document capture and validation inside a mortgage flow is a document-verification / eKYC workload at scale. Printec's digital onboarding and eKYC line is relevant, but BCR builds most of the front end at Erste Group level, so the sellable layer is identity and document-authenticity verification behind the app, not the app.
signals.followup: Identify the identity/document-verification vendor behind George's mortgage document validation.

signals.signal: IT investment proxy from the audited FY2025 accounts: gross additions to intangible assets rose to RON 149.76m in 2025 from RON 132.59m in 2024 (+12.9%), split purchased software RON 95.08m, Group-developed software RON 50.45m, licences RON 4.24m. Gross intangible cost reached RON 1,534.1m at 31/12/2025. Software and licences are amortised over 5-10 years.
signals.source_name: BCR Raport anual 2025, note on Imobilizari necorporale (BVB infocont)
signals.implies: About EUR 29m a year of software capitalisation, growing, on a 5-10 year amortisation life. Sets a realistic ceiling for a software-led engagement and shows BCR capitalises rather than expenses software - so a licence-plus-implementation structure that can be capitalised is easier to land than pure opex on the software side, even though the hardware/service side favours opex.
signals.followup: Derived from the gross-cost rollforward table (row labels were lost in PDF text extraction) - re-confirm against the FY2026 report.

signals.signal: BNR payment statistics reported for 31/12/2025: 11,136 ATMs deployed by resident payment service providers, up 1,108 versus June 2025; 729,408 POS terminals (+161,396); 685,731 EFTPOS acceptance points (+120,300); 28.63 million active cards (+10.07%), of which 24.68 million with a cash function.
signals.implies: The national ATM estate GREW by over 1,100 units in H2 2025 while BCR's shrank by 250 in H1 2026. BCR is ceding physical cash-access share (its 1,669 devices are roughly 15% of the national estate) - which both pressures BCR to defend coverage cheaply (managed services, off-site partnership) and opens white space for independent deployers. POS growth of 161k in six months is the parallel Printec POS/acquiring opportunity.
signals.followup: Re-read the underlying BNR statistics table directly (bnr.ro StatisticsReportHTML) to replace this press citation with the regulator source.

signals.signal: BCR raised RON 1bn in senior non-preferred bonds in June 2026, which BCR describes as the largest corporate issue on the Bucharest Stock Exchange so far this year, oversubscribed in under 24 hours with an order book double the announced minimum. Press reports a 7-year tenor at a 7.77% coupon.
signals.source_name: BCR press release, 15/06/2026, plus BCR H1 2026 release
signals.implies: Funding is not the constraint on capex - the cost/income target is. Confirms BCR could fund a fleet refresh outright if the business case holds, so the sale is about payback, not affordability.
signals.followup: The 7.77% coupon and 7-year tenor come from press (Romania Insider), not read on the BCR release itself.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed). Angles used, deliberately varied from prior runs: (1) BCR's own RO-language press releases, enumerated via https://www.bcr.ro/sitemap.xml after the JS-rendered press index returned no links; (2) the official H1 2026 results PDF on the erstegroup CDN; (3) Erste Group's H1 2026 interim report PDF, text-extracted locally with pdfminer - this is where the ROBOR fine amount, the Romania segment P&L and the BCR headcount came from; (4) BCR's audited FY2025 annual report filed to the Bucharest Stock Exchange infocont system; (5) NEW SOURCE ENVIRONMENT NOT USED BEFORE - BCR's undocumented GEM locations JSON API behind the branch/ATM locator, paged in full to produce an exact, dated census of 1,096 ATMs, 573 MFMs and 284 branches with per-device service tags (voice, contactless, EUR, MoneyGram) and per-branch tags (cashless, teller counter, 24/7 self-service, business deposit, video advisory); (6) Romanian legal database Lege5 for the Law 232/2022 accessibility deadlines; (7) BNR payment statistics via press. BASELINE CORRECTIONS: the baseline's '~2,000 self-service machines / ~955 ATMs; 290 branches' is superseded - as at 30/07/2026 BCR itself states 284 retail units, 74% cashless, 1,750 devices, 19 corporate centres and 15 mobile offices, and the API shows the actual split is 1,096 ATMs + 573 MFMs. The 2016-vintage '1,927 ATM / 79 MFM / 529 APT / 160 ASV' breakdown flagged as stale in the baseline is now definitively replaced by a live census and should be dropped. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the ATM/MFM hardware OEM at BCR is still not publicly identified anywhere - the only vendor evidence is the 2018 NCR/Printec APTRA OptiSuite software project; (b) no public re-confirmation of the OptiSuite/OptiCash contract exists for 2019-2026, so its current status is unknown; (c) no 2026 BCR statement on branch-format modernisation was found - the only branch-transformation announcements are 2018 (28 cashless conversions, EUR 50m over two years) and 2020, both too old to carry; (d) BCR is a private bank and does not publish tenders in SEAP/e-licitatie, so no procurement pipeline is visible; (e) BCR's ESG/annual report does not disclose ATM energy or device counts at a level that would reveal the fleet vendor.
access_issues: consiliulconcurentei.ro/comunicate-de-presa returned HTTP 503 to the fetch tool - not retried further because Erste's own interim report carries the fine figure with more precision (RON 577,361,887). bcr.ro/en/press/press-release and the branch locator page are JS-rendered and return zero links in raw HTML even with a desktop User-Agent; worked around by parsing https://www.bcr.ro/sitemap.xml (840 KB, RO+EN URLs) and by calling the underlying GEM locations JSON API directly. https://www.bcr.ro/en/sitemap.xml returns a 404 page. The first guessed H1 2026 press-release URL 404'd before the sitemap route resolved it. zfenglish.com is paywalled ('To read the full story, please login') - not used for any figure. Both large PDFs (Erste H1 2026, 1.7 MB; BCR FY2025 annual report, 7.8 MB) were downloaded with curl and text-extracted locally with pdfminer rather than through the fetch tool.
operator_requests: none - every source cited was opened successfully.
